architecture: ZK-rollup on Ethereum mainnet. Custom Plonky2 circuits. Single centralized sequencer.

UpgradeGatekeeper.note: Controls upgrades. L2Beat: no delay on upgrades — CRITICAL.

prover_source.note: ZK prover and desert exit circuits open source. Audited by ZKSecurity.

upgrade_gatekeeper.source: L2Beat: 'Funds can be stolen if a contract receives a malicious code upgrade. There is no delay on code upgrades (CRITICAL).'

funds_location.note: User funds held in ZkLighter core contract on Ethereum mainnet.

contracts_verified.note: Core contracts verified on Etherscan. ZK prover and desert exit circuit code open source on GitHub.

chain_l2beat_stage.note: 5 of required conditions met. Blocked from Stage 1 by no-delay upgrade key (UpgradeGatekeeper).

upgrade_delay_seconds.note: UpgradeGatekeeper has no timelock. Instant upgrade = instant fund loss risk.

lp_exit.note: Lighter does not use a public LP vault model in the same sense as EVM perp DEXes. Maker/market-maker positions managed via centralized sequencer.

trader_exit.mechanism: Priority queue submission on Ethereum L1 → sequencer must process within 14 days or Desert Mode activates → user generates ZK proof of balance → withdraws directly from contract
trader_exit.censorship_resistance: Desert Mode: if sequencer ignores priority queue for 14 days, rollup freezes and users can exit with self-generated ZK proofs. Open source circuit code available at github.com/elliottech/lighter-prover.

can_user_exit_unilaterally.qualifier: conditional — requires 14-day wait + self-generating a ZK proof of balance. Desert Mode is the mechanism. NOT instant. Upgrade key risk remains: if contract is upgraded before Desert Mode triggers, funds can be lost.

exit_function.value: Priority queue → Desert Mode withdrawal with self-generated ZK proof

exit_depends_on.value: sequencer (normal), UpgradeGatekeeper EOA (critical risk), ZK circuit correctness (for desert exit)

forced_inclusion.mechanism: Desert Mode after 14-day sequencer non-response to priority queue

alternative_frontend.note: Contracts are verified; technically a permissionless frontend is possible but none documented.
